site.name: Little Maud Mine
overview: Little Maud Mine is a named inactive gold-and-silver mine in Boulder County's Magnolia Mining District.

USGS-derived topographic place data preserves the mine at approximately 39.994708, -105.364438, providing a stable mine-level identification point without implying that a surviving shaft or portal has been field-verified.

timeline.text: Little Maud Mine formed part of the Magnolia Mining District, a compact Boulder County gold-telluride district whose principal veins were discovered during the late nineteenth century.
USGS-derived Eldorado Springs topographic mapping retains Little Maud Mine as a named inactive mine feature.

moreHistory: The retained mine coordinate is 39.9947083, -105.3644377. Remnant uses this documented mine-level locality for identification and does not claim that the point marks a surviving opening surveyed in the field.
Mindat's Magnolia Mining District locality index independently lists Little Maud Mine within the district, helping distinguish this Boulder County site from same-named mines elsewhere in Colorado.
A focused exact-site media search did not locate a rights-cleared reusable Little Maud Mine photograph; nearby Magnolia-district images were rejected rather than attached to the wrong site.
